title_en: Guiding Case No. 259: Beijing Fengtai District Mou Environmental Research Institute v. Jiangsu Mougang Group Co., Ltd. — civil public interest litigation for environmental pollution
ruling_gist_en:
1. In environmental civil public interest litigation cases, when the plaintiff applies for withdrawal of the lawsuit, the people's court may only grant the withdrawal upon review and confirmation that the plaintiff's claims concerning the defendant's assumption of ecological environment restoration, damage compensation liability, and other claims involving social public interests have been fully satisfied.

2. The 'full satisfaction of the plaintiff's claims' as stipulated in Article 26 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Environmental Civil Public Interest Litigation Cases refers to the full satisfaction of the plaintiff's claims involving social public interests.

full_text_en:
Guiding Case No. 259

Beijing Fengtai District Mou Environmental Research Institute v. Jiangsu Mou Steel Group Co., Ltd. — dispute over civil public interest litigation for environmental pollution

(Discussed and adopted by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court on May 26, 2025)

Keywords: civil; civil public interest litigation for environmental pollution; social public interest; review of withdrawal of lawsuit

Ruling Gist

1. In a civil environmental public interest litigation case, where the plaintiff applies to withdraw the lawsuit, the people's court may only grant the withdrawal upon confirmation that the plaintiff's claims concerning social public interests, such as the defendant's assumption of ecological environment restoration and damage compensation liability, have been fully realized.

2. "All claims of the plaintiff have been fully realized" as stipulated in Article 26 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Environmental Civil Public Interest Litigation Cases means that all claims of the plaintiff involving social public interests have been fully realized.

Basic Facts

On June 28, 2018, the Ministry of Ecology and Environment reported the issue of one million tons of steel slag stockpiling by Jiangsu Mou Steel Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jiangsu Mou Steel Group). The steel slag storage yard within its subsidiary's plant area was not designed strictly in accordance with the requirements of the "Standard for Pollution Control on the Storage and Disposal Site for General Industrial Solid Wastes" (GB18599-2001), and was not equipped with supporting pollution prevention and control facilities, posing a significant risk of environmental pollution. At the same time, Jiangsu Mou Steel Group also had acts of discharging air pollutants exceeding standards.

On March 15, 2019, Beijing Fengtai District Mou Environmental Research Institute (hereinafter referred to as Fengtai Mou Environmental Research Institute) filed a civil public interest litigation for environmental pollution with the Suzhou Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province, asserting that Jiangsu Mou Steel Group's pollution of the environment had caused damage and should bear tort liability. It requested the court to order Jiangsu Mou Steel Group to: 1. Cease the infringement, immediately stop the discharge of smoke, dust, and exhaust gases exceeding standards, and stop illegal acts such as the improper stacking of waste residues and waste that harm the environmental public interest; 2. Make an apology, and publicly apologize to the public on national mainstream media for the continuous acts harming the environmental public interest; 3. Eliminate the danger, take effective measures to eliminate the environmental risks to the public interest, such as the risk of smoke, dust, and exhaust gases to the atmospheric environment and the risk of waste residues and waste to the Yangtze River water environment; 4. Compensate for losses, compensate for the losses caused by the loss of service functions from the time the environment was damaged until the completion of restoration; 5. Bear the inspection and appraisal fees, reasonable attorney fees, and travel and other expenses incurred by the plaintiff for the litigation; 6. Bear all litigation costs of this case.

During the trial of the case, on April 19, 2019, Fengtai Mou Environmental Research Institute applied to withdraw the lawsuit on the grounds that the government might initiate ecological environment damage compensation work concerning the environmental pollution involved. The Suzhou Intermediate People's Court, after trial, held that the reasons for withdrawal given by Fengtai Mou Environmental Research Institute did not comply with the provisions of relevant judicial interpretations, and therefore, on October 22, 2019, rendered the civil ruling (2019) Su 05 Min Chu No. 299-1: not permitting Fengtai Mou Environmental Research Institute to withdraw the lawsuit.

On October 17, 2019, the People's Government of Zhangjiagang City, Jiangsu Province, sent a letter to the Suzhou Intermediate People's Court: The People's Government of Zhangjiagang City, authorized by the Suzhou Municipal People's Government, was handling the ecological environment damage compensation work of Jiangsu Mou Steel Group and had initiated consultations on ecological environment damage compensation. The Suzhou Intermediate People's Court considered that the outcome of the consultations between the Zhangjiagang Municipal People's Government and Jiangsu Mou Steel Group regarding the ecological environment damage compensation involved in the case might affect the trial of this case, and therefore, on October 29, 2019, rendered the civil ruling (2019) Su 05 Min Chu No. 299-2: suspending the proceedings of this case.

After assessment, the ecological environment damage amount caused by the pollution acts of Jiangsu Mou Steel Group involved in the case was RMB 40,349,639.59. On December 5, 2020, the Zhangjiagang Municipal People's Government and Jiangsu Mou Steel Group, through consultations, reached the "Ecological Environment Damage Compensation Agreement" and a supplementary agreement, and applied to the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province (which, with the approval of the Supreme People's Court, established the Nanjing Environmental Resources Tribunal in June 2019 to centrally accept environmental resource cases within the jurisdiction of intermediate people's courts in Jiangsu Province) for judicial confirmation. The Nanjing Intermediate People's Court, after review, held that the soil pollution damage caused by the steel slag involved in the case had been effectively restored, the risk of groundwater pollution had been eliminated, the compensation for atmospheric pollution damage had been fully paid, and the "Ecological Environment Damage Compensation Agreement" and the supplementary agreement involved in the case could achieve the effect of restoring the ecological environment and compensating for the ecological environment damage, and the responsibility mechanism determined in the agreements could ensure their performance. Therefore, on June 4, 2021, it rendered the civil ruling (2021) Su 01 Min Te No. 64, confirming that the "Ecological Environment Damage Compensation Agreement" and the supplementary agreement reached between the Zhangjiagang Municipal People's Government and Jiangsu Mou Steel Group on December 5, 2020, were lawful and effective.

On February 23, 2021, Fengtai Mou Environmental Research Institute applied to withdraw the lawsuit for the second time, on the grounds that the case had been handled through the local ecological environment damage compensation consultation procedure and a compensation agreement had been reached.

Judgment

Given that all claims of the Beijing Fengtai District Mou Environmental Research Institute involving social public interests had been fully realized, the Suzhou Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province rendered the civil ruling (2019) Su 05 Min Chu No. 299 on June 5, 2021: permitting the Beijing Fengtai District Mou Environmental Research Institute to withdraw the lawsuit.

Reasoning

The focus of the dispute in this case is: whether all claims of Fengtai Mou Environmental Research Institute have been fully realized, and whether its application for withdrawal of the lawsuit should be permitted.

Article 145, paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (2017 Amendment) provides: "Before a judgment is pronounced, whether to permit a plaintiff to withdraw the lawsuit shall be determined by the people's court by ruling." In environmental civil public interest litigation, the subject matter of the lawsuit involves the environmental public interest, and the plaintiff's exercise of the right to withdraw the lawsuit must be premised on not harming the social public interest. Where a plaintiff applies to withdraw the lawsuit, the people's court shall, ex officio, review it and only permit the withdrawal upon confirming that it will not harm the social public interest. In this regard, Article 26 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Environmental Civil Public Interest Litigation Cases (Fa Shi [2015] No. 1, 2020 Amendment) provides: "Where a department responsible for the supervision and administration of environmental resource protection, in accordance with the law, fulfills its supervisory duties, resulting in all claims of the plaintiff being fully realized, and the plaintiff applies to withdraw the lawsuit, the people's court shall permit it." During the trial of this case, upon learning that the government might initiate ecological environment damage compensation work concerning the environmental pollution involved, Fengtai Mou Environmental Research Institute applied to the people's court for withdrawal of the lawsuit for the first time on April 19, 2019. After review, the people's court considered that the environmental pollution problem involved in the case had not yet been actually resolved, there was no evidence proving that all claims of the plaintiff Fengtai Mou Environmental Research Institute involving social public interests had been fully realized, and permitting the plaintiff to withdraw the lawsuit might harm the social public interest. Therefore, it ruled not to permit the withdrawal of the lawsuit.

Thereafter, the Zhangjiagang Municipal People's Government, as the government consultation handling institution designated by the Suzhou Municipal People's Government for ecological environment damage compensation, reached the "Ecological Environment Damage Compensation Agreement" and a supplementary agreement with Jiangsu Mou Steel Group through consultations regarding the pollution involved in the case. To ensure the public's right to know and participate, the content of the agreement was publicly announced in accordance with the law. On June 4, 2021, the above agreements were confirmed lawful and effective by the civil ruling (2021) Su 01 Min Te No. 64 of the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court. During this period, on February 23, 2021, Fengtai Mou Environmental Research Institute applied for withdrawal of the lawsuit for the second time.

Upon review, Jiangsu Mou Steel Group had already carried out rectification measures regarding the environmental pollution problem involved in the case. After appraisal and assessment and review by the Suzhou Environmental Protection Inspection and Rectification Work Team, it was confirmed that the pollution problem had been rectified and met the standards. In this case, the plaintiff's claims involving social public interests, such as requesting the defendant Jiangsu Mou Steel Group to cease the infringement, eliminate the danger, and compensate for losses, had been fully realized after the ecological environment damage compensation consultation.

For the phrase "all claims of the plaintiff have been fully realized" in Article 26 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Environmental Civil Public Interest Litigation Cases, it should be understood as all claims of the plaintiff involving social public interests have been fully realized. In this case, the plaintiff's claims for requiring the defendant to bear attorney fees, travel expenses, and other expenses incurred for the litigation, as well as litigation costs, only involve the plaintiff's own interests and do not involve social public interests; before these claims are realized, the plaintiff's application to withdraw the lawsuit is an exercise of its civil rights and litigation rights within the scope provided by law. Therefore, the grounds for Fengtai Mou Environmental Research Institute's second application to withdraw the lawsuit comply with the provisions of the law, and the people's court should permit it.

Relevant Legal Provisions

Articles 1234 and 1235 of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China

Articles 148 and 153 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (the version applicable to this case is the 2017 Amendment of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 145 and 150)

Articles 22, 26, and 27 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Environmental Civil Public Interest Litigation Cases (Fa Shi [2015] No. 1, 2020 Amendment)
